## Architectures

<a id="bitdance"></a>

### BitDance

Decoder-only autoregressive transformer (initialized from Qwen3-14B for text-to-image) over binary visual tokens, with a lightweight-DiT binary diffusion head that samples each p×p patch of tokens jointly in continuous space (next-patch diffusion).

BitDance (ByteDance with CUHK and other institutions) is an autoregressive image generator whose visual tokens are binary vectors from a lookup-free quantization tokenizer with vocabularies up to 2^256 states. Because a softmax over that many indices is impractical, a small DiT-style diffusion head treats each token as a vertex of a hypercube, generates it with rectified-flow sampling in continuous space conditioned on the transformer's hidden state, and snaps the result back to ±1. The same head samples a whole p×p patch of tokens at once (next-patch diffusion), under a block-wise causal mask, so many tokens are produced per step. For text-to-image generation a 14B model initialized from Qwen3-14B serves as both text encoder and image generator, uses a 16×-downsampling tokenizer and generates up to 1024×1024 images, with 16 or, after a short distillation stage, 64 tokens per step; the paper reports over 30× speedup over prior next-token AR models at 1024px.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14041) · [GitHub](https://github.com/shallowdream204/BitDance) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/shallowdream204/BitDance-14B-64x)

![BitDance — Figure 4 (PDF p. 6)](../assets/architectures/bitdance.png)

*Figure 4 (PDF p. 6) · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14041)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T → I · **Interaction:** generation

The token sequence is [bos] text [boi] [res_i] [res_j] visual tokens [eoi] [eos], where the two resolution tokens fix the token grid; p²−1 learnable prefix tokens allow the first patch to be predicted in parallel, and 2D sinusoidal position embeddings are added to the LLM's 1D RoPE. Text-to-image training uses pre-training and continued training on open datasets such as LAION, SFT data including images generated by other models, a small amount of image-to-text data to preserve text understanding, and mixed 256/512/1024px resolutions. Although the tokens are discrete, sampling uses a continuous diffusion head, so the model is grouped with continuous-token AR models. The paper also reports class-conditional ImageNet models (e.g. FID 1.24). Code is Apache-2.0 on GitHub; the BitDance-14B-16x and BitDance-14B-64x model cards list apache-2.0, and three binary tokenizers are released.

**License:** code: Apache-2.0; weights: apache-2.0.

**Variants:** BitDance-14B-16x; BitDance-14B-64x.

</details>

<a id="dart"></a>

### DART

Denoising autoregressive transformer: a Llama-style decoder over continuous VAE latent patches that predicts each less-noisy image from the whole sequence of previous noisy images (non-Markovian diffusion), with cross-attention to T5-XL text features.

DART (Apple, with CUHK and Mila) merges autoregression and diffusion. Instead of denoising from only the current noisy image, as Markovian diffusion does, its transformer sees the concatenated sequence of all earlier noisy versions of the image and predicts the next, cleaner one, using a chunk-based causal mask and KV caching like a language model; no image quantization is involved. Two extensions add token-level autoregression inside each denoising step (DART-AR) and a small flow-matching head that models each token's distribution (DART-FM). Matryoshka-DART handles several resolutions in one sequence, and Kaleido-DART jointly trains discrete text-token prediction. Text-to-image models are trained on CC12M, mostly at 256×256 with 512×512 fine-tuning for Matryoshka-DART.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.08159) · GitHub: no author-linked repository found

![DART — Figure 2](../assets/architectures/dart.png)

*Figure 2 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.08159)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T → I · **Interaction:** generation

Images are encoded with the Stable Diffusion v1.4 VAE (sd-vae-ft-ema), patchified with patch size 2 into 256 tokens of 16 channels; T = 16 denoising steps with a cosine-derived schedule. Blocks use RoPE and SwiGLU; class-conditional models use AdaLN, which text-to-image models replace with cross-attention over a pretrained T5-XL encoder, and no timestep embedding is needed. DART-FM adds a 3-layer MLP flow network (about 1% more parameters) with 100 flow-matching steps between autoregressive steps. The paper also reports class-conditional ImageNet results. No author-linked code was found; a third-party reimplementation exists on GitHub but is not an official source.

**Variants:** DART-AR; DART-FM; Matryoshka-DART; Kaleido-DART.

</details>

<a id="fluid"></a>

### Fluid

Random-order (masked) autoregressive transformer over continuous VAE tokens with a per-token MLP diffusion head, conditioned on frozen T5-XXL text features through cross-attention.

Fluid (Google DeepMind and MIT) studies why autoregressive image models scale worse than language models by comparing discrete versus continuous tokens and raster versus random generation order in a controlled text-to-image setup. Continuous tokens gave clearly better visual quality, and random-order models with bidirectional attention scored higher on GenEval than raster-order causal models, so the final Fluid model combines both: it predicts masked continuous tokens in random order, one or several at a time, and models each token with a small diffusion head following the MAR diffusion-loss approach. The largest model has 10.5B parameters and is trained on WebLI at 256×256.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13863) · GitHub: no author-linked repository found

![Fluid — Figure 3](../assets/architectures/fluid.png)

*Figure 3 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13863)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T → I · **Interaction:** generation

Images are encoded with a Stable Diffusion KL autoencoder into 32×32×4 latents, grouped into 2×2 patches to give 256 tokens of 16 channels. Text (up to 128 tokens) is embedded by a frozen 4.7B T5-XXL encoder followed by a six-block trainable text aligner. Each transformer block applies self-attention and an MLP to visual tokens and cross-attention from visual to text tokens; unknown tokens are replaced by a learnable mask token. The six-layer MLP diffusion head uses a cosine schedule with 1000 training steps resampled to 100 at inference. The paper's scaling study also trains discrete-token (VQ) and raster-order variants from 150M to 3B parameters. No code or weights were found linked from the paper.

</details>

<a id="glm-image"></a>

### GLM-Image

Autoregressive–diffusion hybrid: a 9B autoregressive generator initialized from GLM-4-9B-0414 predicts discrete semantic-VQ image tokens, and a 7B single-stream DiT flow-matching decoder (following CogView4) renders them into a latent image.

GLM-Image (Z.ai) splits image generation into a semantic stage and a detail stage. The autoregressive part, built on the GLM-4-9B-0414 language model with an added vision embedding layer and a vision LM head, generates semantic-VQ tokens from the X-Omni tokenizer scheme; it first produces about 256 low-resolution layout tokens and then 1K–4K higher-resolution tokens. A 7B single-stream DiT decoder trained with flow matching receives these tokens, projected and concatenated with the VAE latent along the channel dimension, and adds the high-frequency detail; it needs no prompt text encoder, only a lightweight Glyph-ByT5 module for rendering text in the image. Final outputs range from 1024 to 2048 px. The same model also handles image-to-image tasks such as editing, style transfer and identity-preserving or multi-subject generation, and both stages are post-trained separately with GRPO-based reinforcement learning.

[Announcement](https://z.ai/blog/glm-image) · [GitHub](https://github.com/zai-org/GLM-Image) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-Image)

![GLM-Image — README architecture figure (architecture_1)](../assets/architectures/glm-image.png)

*README architecture figure (architecture_1) · [Source](https://github.com/zai-org/GLM-Image)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → I · **Interaction:** editing

Unlike most entries in this group, the autoregressive stage predicts discrete (semantic-VQ) tokens; GLM-Image is listed here as an AR–diffusion hybrid. The AR model uses MRoPE for interleaved text and images, freezes the text word embeddings, and is trained in 256px, 512px and mixed 512–1024px stages (16× tokenizer compression); preliminary low-resolution tokens receive a higher training weight. For editing, both semantic-VQ tokens and VAE latents of reference images condition the decoder, with block-causal attention between reference and generated images. The decoder is RL-tuned with flow-GRPO using LPIPS, OCR and hand-quality rewards; the AR module uses HPSv3, OCR and VLM rewards. No paper was found; the date is that of the developer's technical blog, which renders it as 2026-01-14. Code is Apache-2.0 on GitHub, and the Hugging Face model card lists MIT for the weights; an API is also offered.

**License:** code: Apache-2.0; weights: MIT.

</details>

<a id="hart"></a>

### HART

Hybrid autoregressive model: a scalable-resolution VAR-style next-scale transformer predicts discrete multi-scale tokens, and a 37M-parameter residual diffusion MLP predicts the continuous residual that is added to form the final latent tokens.

HART (Hybrid Autoregressive Transformer, from MIT, NVIDIA and Tsinghua) generates 1024×1024 images directly with an autoregressive model. Its hybrid tokenizer splits an autoencoder's continuous latent into the sum of discrete multi-scale VAR tokens, which capture overall structure, and a continuous residual that holds fine detail. A VAR-style transformer predicts the discrete tokens scale by scale, with text tokens from a frozen Qwen2-1.5B language model concatenated in front and visible to all visual tokens, and a lightweight MLP diffusion head predicts the residual in 8 sampling steps, conditioned on the transformer's final hidden states and the last discrete tokens. The paper reports quality comparable to diffusion models of similar size with 4.5–7.7× higher throughput.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10812) · [GitHub](https://github.com/mit-han-lab/hart) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/mit-han-lab/hart-0.7b-1024px)

![HART — Figure 6](../assets/architectures/hart.png)

*Figure 6 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10812)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T → I · **Interaction:** generation

The hybrid tokenizer is initialized from a pretrained VAR tokenizer and trained alternately to decode both continuous and discrete latents; only continuous latents are decoded at inference. For text-to-image generation the paper starts from its 1B class-conditional configuration with Llama-style blocks and removes all AdaLN layers (a 30% parameter reduction; the released model is HART-0.7B at 1024px). VAR's absolute position embeddings are replaced with sinusoidal step embeddings and 1D/2D rotary embeddings so low-resolution checkpoints can be fine-tuned to 1024px; about 80% of tokens are dropped from residual-diffusion supervision during training. The paper names Qwen2-1.5B as the text encoder, while the README downloads Qwen2-VL-1.5B-Instruct. Class-conditional ImageNet models are also reported. Code (GitHub) and the hart-0.7b-1024px weights (Hugging Face) are MIT-licensed.

**License:** code: MIT; weights: MIT.

**Variants:** HART-0.7B-1024px.

</details>

<a id="jetformer"></a>

### JetFormer

Decoder-only Gemma-style transformer that autoregressively models text tokens and continuous soft image tokens produced by a jointly trained normalizing flow ("jet") on raw pixels, with a Gaussian-mixture output head for image tokens.

JetFormer (Google DeepMind) is trained end to end to maximize the likelihood of raw images and text, with no separately pretrained image encoder, VAE or tokenizer. A transformer-based normalizing flow maps image patches losslessly to soft tokens; the same flow serves as image encoder for understanding and, inverted, as image decoder for generation. The autoregressive transformer predicts text tokens with a softmax and soft image tokens with a Gaussian mixture, trained on WebLI image-text pairs in both orders so that one model does text-to-image generation and image-to-text tasks such as captioning and VQA at 256×256. A noise curriculum that adds strong pixel noise early in training steers the model toward high-level image structure.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.19722) · [GitHub](https://github.com/google-research/big_vision)

![JetFormer — Figure 1 (PDF p. 2)](../assets/architectures/jetformer.png)

*Figure 1 (PDF p. 2) · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.19722)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → I, T · **Interaction:** generation

The flow uses 32 affine coupling blocks with channel-wise splitting, each built from ViT blocks of width 512, over 16×16 patches; redundant dimensions can be factored out of the autoregressive model (via a learnable invertible linear map, with PCA explored as an alternative), leaving 128 of 768 dimensions per patch. The GMM head uses 1024 mixtures with diagonal covariance, and classifier-free guidance is applied at sampling. Backbone sizes of 350M, 750M and 1.3B parameters are studied; class-conditional ImageNet models are also reported. The noise curriculum is a training-time augmentation, not iterative denoising at inference. Training configs are published in the Apache-2.0 google-research/big_vision repository (big_vision/configs/proj/jetformer), which the paper links as its code; no released weights were found. The model also fits the unified group because it documents image understanding; it is catalogued here as a continuous-token autoregressive model.

**License:** code: Apache-2.0.

**Variants:** JetFormer-B; JetFormer-M; JetFormer-L.

</details>

<a id="nextstep-1"></a>

### NextStep-1

Causal decoder-only transformer initialized from Qwen2.5-14B that predicts the next continuous image token (a 2×2-packed patch of a Flux-VAE-derived latent) through a 157M-parameter patch-wise flow-matching MLP head, alongside a standard LM head for text.

NextStep-1 (StepFun) applies plain next-token prediction to a sequence of discrete text tokens followed by continuous image tokens, without vector quantization and without a large diffusion decoder. A 14B causal transformer, initialized from Qwen2.5-14B and using standard 1D RoPE, reads the prompt and previously generated image patches; its hidden state conditions a small MLP flow-matching head that turns noise into the next image patch. Images come from a tokenizer fine-tuned from the FLUX.1-dev VAE, whose 16-channel latents are channel-normalized and noise-perturbed during training to keep the latent space robust, then packed 2×2 into 64-channel tokens. An editing model (NextStep-1-Large-Edit) extends the same architecture to instruction-based image editing, and the later NextStep-1.1 release adds extended training and flow-based RL post-training.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.10711) · [GitHub](https://github.com/stepfun-ai/NextStep-1) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/stepfun-ai/NextStep-1-Large)

![NextStep-1 — Figure 2](../assets/architectures/nextstep-1.png)

*Figure 2 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.10711)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → I · **Interaction:** editing

The multimodal sequence is formatted as text, an <image_area>h*w metadata token, then <boi> image tokens <eoi>; text hidden states go to the LM head with cross-entropy and image hidden states to the flow-matching head (12 layers, hidden size 1536). The tokenizer uses 8× spatial downsampling, so a 256×256 image becomes 256 tokens. Released checkpoints (Aug 2025) are NextStep-1-Large-Pretrain, NextStep-1-Large and NextStep-1-Large-Edit; NextStep-1.1 and NextStep-1.1-Pretrain followed in December 2025 per the README, and training code was released in February 2026. Code is Apache-2.0 on GitHub and the Hugging Face model cards list apache-2.0.

**License:** code: Apache-2.0; weights: apache-2.0.

**Variants:** NextStep-1-Large; NextStep-1-Large-Pretrain; NextStep-1-Large-Edit; NextStep-1.1.

</details>

<a id="starflow"></a>

### STARFlow

Latent normalizing flow built from transformer autoregressive flow (TARFlow) blocks in a deep-shallow design: one deep causal transformer flow block conditioned on the prompt, followed by a few shallow 2-layer flow blocks, over pretrained-autoencoder latents with a fine-tuned decoder.

STARFlow (Apple) shows that normalizing flows can scale to high-resolution text-to-image generation. The model is a single invertible flow trained by exact maximum likelihood on continuous autoencoder latents, without quantization or iterative denoising. Each flow block is an autoregressive transformer; almost all capacity sits in one deep block that behaves like a Gaussian language model over latent tokens and is the only block that sees the caption, while a few cheap shallow blocks refine local detail. Sampling runs the deep block autoregressively from Gaussian noise, then the shallow blocks, and a decoder fine-tuned on noise-injected latents maps the result to pixels. A revised classifier-free guidance algorithm for autoregressive flows improves quality at high guidance weights. The text-to-image model has 3.8B parameters and supports variable aspect ratios.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06276) · [GitHub](https://github.com/apple-aiml-research/ml-starflow) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/apple/starflow)

![STARFlow — Figure 4 (PDF p. 5)](../assets/architectures/starflow.png)

*Figure 4 (PDF p. 5) · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06276)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → I · **Interaction:** editing

Text conditioning uses a T5-XL encoder; a variant initializes the deep block from the Gemma2 LLM and needs no separate text encoder. Blocks follow the Llama 3 setup with RoPE; latents are modeled with patch size 1 (e.g. the SD-1.4 autoencoder maps 256×256 images to 32×32 latents), and Gaussian noise is added to latents during training, which the jointly fine-tuned decoder learns to remove. Models are pre-trained at 256×256 on 400M images (text-to-image models are trained either on CC12M alone or, in the scaled setting, on an in-house dataset plus CC12M totalling about 700M pairs) with mixed-resolution fine-tuning over 9 aspect-ratio buckets. The paper also shows training-free inpainting and a variant fine-tuned for instruction-based editing, plus class-conditional ImageNet models. The official apple-aiml-research/ml-starflow repository (apple/ml-starflow redirects there) provides training and sampling code under an Apple software license and a starflow_3B_t2i_256x256 checkpoint on Hugging Face under the Apple Machine Learning Research Model license (apple-amlr, research use only); the repository also hosts the separate STARFlow-V video model.

**License:** weights: apple-amlr.

**Variants:** STARFlow 3.8B (T5-XL); STARFlow with Gemma2-initialized deep block.

</details>
